result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens sends a POST to process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with body containing only calcomUserId and appSlug — no Authorization header, no secret, no signature. The endpoint returns live OAuth tokens for a caller-supplied userId. This is verifiable directly in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts. Lack of authentication on the outbound sync request is a real security defect in the introduced code.

judged_text: The outbound token sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication at all (no secret, signature, or credential) despite the endpoint handing back live OAuth access tokens for a caller-supplied `calcomUserId`, and userIds are small sequential integers trivially enumerable — anyone who can reach the endpoint can steal access tokens for arbitrary users

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Cal.com POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication material (no secret header, signature, etc.). That part of the finding is directly supported by the diff. However, the claim that “anyone who can reach the endpoint can steal access tokens” depends on how the *external* endpoint is implemented and exposed, which is not shown here. The diff does introduce an unauthenticated call pattern that is a concrete security/architecture concern for this feature, but the full exploitability is not verifiable from the PR alone.
